items.text: **Check blood glucose level in ANY patient with signs or symptoms consistent with hypoglycemia**
Examples: *Altered mental status, agitation, focal neurologic deficit, seizure, weakness, diaphoresis, decreased motor tone, pallor*
Blood glucose level < 60 mg/dl
If newly born refer to [[p:3020|neonatal resuscitation]] protocol
If patient can safely tolerate, administer [[m:9240|oral glucose]]
*(intact gag reflex, follows verbal commands)*
If oral glucose contraindicated or symptoms unresolved, administer [[m:9090|dextrose]] IV
If unable to establish IV:
Administer [[m:9130|glucagon]]
Alternative: If severe symptoms (coma), consider [[p:1060|IO]] and administer [[m:9090|dextrose]] IO
If still symptomatic, recheck blood glucose level and consider other causes of [[p:4010|altered mental status]]
Monitor and transport or **Contact Receiving Hospital** for refusal if indicated
If hypoglycemia still most likely despite normal reading on glucometer, administer glucose **regardless**, while considering other causes of altered mental status

sidebars.title: Regarding refusals after a hypoglycemic episode:

items.text: See [[p:0032|patient refusal]] protocol
Transport is always indicated for any of the following patients:
With *unexplained* hypoglycemia
Taking oral hypoglycemic meds
Not taking food by mouth
Do not have competent adult to monitor
In general, treat the patient, not the glucose value. Treat shock if present.
Consider normal saline bolus for patients with hyperglycemia and no evidence of fluid overload.
Pediatric patients with concern for DKA should not exceed 10-20 mL/kg of fluids.
